chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The fasting person immerses himself in water and does not rub his head."
ai.seo_question: Does a fasting person break their fast by immersing in water and rubbing their head?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the boundaries of *ghusl* (ritual bath) for a fasting person, distinguishing between permissible full immersion and the specific act of rubbing the head (*ramus*). Scholars interpret *ramus* as vigorously rubbing the head to dislodge water, which may cause it to reach the throat and break the fast, highlighting the Shia emphasis on precaution (*ihtiyat*) in maintaining ritual purity without invalidating the fast.
